business_type: cyclical (capital-markets franchise at a cycle peak)
moat_source: franchise position and talent network in advisory/trading (top of league tables for decades); evidence: 19.8% ROE and record GBM revenue - but the earnings stream itself is the most cyclical in large-cap finance

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% of the gap closed by year 3. Excludes the ~2% dividend yield. Earnings used as the cash-flow proxy (bank convention); noted as a framework deviation.

primary_model_risk: Peak-earnings capitalization: Q1's $17.55 EPS annualizes to ~$70, but that includes advisory +89% and record trading - textbook cycle-peak conditions. Base case normalizes earnings ~10% below the current run-rate; if the M&A/trading boom mean-reverts to 2023-24 levels instead, the bear case's ~30% earnings decline is the historical norm, not the tail.
expectations_gap_key_variable: cycle permanence: at ~19x trailing (vs the ~10-12x historical bank band) the market caps peak advisory/trading earnings as if structural; our base case pays 12x normalized earnings and lands ~24% below the quote - even the sell side's average target (~978) sits under the market
top_5_bull_arguments: 19.8% ROE with record GBM revenue - execution at the top of the franchise's game
Advisory +89% suggests the M&A cycle is early, not late (bull case logic)
EPS run-rate ~$70 puts the forward multiple near 14.6x - not absurd if earnings hold
Asset & Wealth Management mix shift slowly de-cyclicalizes the earnings base
Capital returns are large and consistent; ~2% yield plus buybacks at high ROE
top_5_bear_arguments: 19x trailing for the most cyclical earnings stream in large-cap finance, at what advisory +89% suggests is the boom quarter
Expected IV ($787) is ~23% below the price; consensus itself is Hold with targets below market
Capital-markets revenue mean-reverts violently - the historical norm after quarters like Q1 is a 25-35% earnings decline
Regulatory capital changes can throttle the buyback with little notice
Nothing in the mix is defensive: banking, trading, and underwriting all peak together
thesis_breakers: Q2 2026 (July 14) advisory or trading revenue down sequentially by >15%
ROE falling below 14% for two consecutive quarters
M&A announced-volume data rolling over (the leading indicator)
Credit-cycle deterioration hitting the financing book
position_size_recommendation: 0% at current price; a franchise to buy at 10x mid-cycle earnings during the next capital-markets winter - not at 19x during the summer
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROA null (not meaningful/sourced for a bank); ROE 19.8 is the reported annualized figure. Earnings are used as the FCF proxy per bank convention - a documented deviation from the framework's FCF DCF, since bank 'FCF' is not a meaningful construct. Revenue/EPS/ROE are reported (8-K) - strong data foundation; the normalization path is judgment.
historical_context: Directional context only - low confidence. Verified datapoints: trailing P/E 19.06, +2.32% past week, consensus Hold with average target ~978 below market (pass1/search). The 10-12x historical bank multiple band is industry convention, not a company-specific sourced range.
